messages:
sara: FYI we got a high-severity from a Dedicated customer — sustained throughput drop and lots of 429s since 18:02 UTC. They say tail latency x3 and token/sec down ~60%. attaching grafana + traces. can eng-runtime triage?

oliver: which pool and model? customer id? any billing/auth errors in the logs?

sara: customer: corp-acme-42, pool: rp-west2-ded-17, model: redwood/gpt-open-13b-8q. autoscale policy min=2 max=10, burst enabled. no auth/billing errors shown. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc/throughput?orgId=1 (screenshot in thread)

raj: seeing the same on our metrics — prefills per-second spiked, but batch sizes dropped. looks like continuous-batcher is pushing many tiny microbatches.

maria: @raj can you paste the sample of the request-size distribution? suspect a prompt-size regression or KV-cache churn.

raj: pasted rough numbers: 
- 95th prompt tokens ~ 24k 
- mean prompt tokens ~ 600 
- observed batch token median ~ 1.2k (should be ~12k)

raj: quick grep from node logs: `batch_window_ms=2 preferrer=continuous_batcher max_batch_tokens=4096 prefill_parallelism=4`

infra-bot: alert: pool rp-west2-ded-17 CPU on scheduler nodes above 75% for 7m; queue_depth spiked from 40->600\.

oliver: customer says they recently rolled a client-side change to add many short tool-calls per request (structured tool outputs). likely changed seq distribution.

sara: they also reported a brief auth 401 earlier but that was resolved — unrelated?

raj: 401 shouldn't affect batching, but the many short tool calls could be fragmenting batches and causing the scheduler to favor latency (small windows). current max_batch_tokens is pretty low for their mix. two angles: (1) ineff batching due to low max_batch_tokens + continuous-batcher draining early, (2) noisy tenant behavior: one tenant doing many tiny requests stealing pack space.

maria: repro plan: run loadgen that emulates their real p50/p95 prompt sizes and tool-call fanout. can we get a short window on the pool for a canary?

oliver: I collected one trace: request_id=acme:7754 path=/v1/generate -> many small subrequests, each prefill then decode. attaching simplified trace snippet: 
```
prefill: 32 token chunks x 20 (avg 640)
kv_cache_miss spikes
batch_closed_early due_to_window_timeout
emit small batches (batch_size 1-3)
```

raj: suggested config to test (safe canary): 
```
# increase max batch token ceiling and batching window
max_batch_tokens: 16384
batch_window_ms: 6
prefill_parallelism: 8
fairqueue_weights: default -> tenant-isolation higher for corp-acme-42
```

raj: rationale: increasing max_batch_tokens lets the scheduler pack more tokens into each microbatch when many small prompts exist; batch_window_ms up a bit gives scheduler breathing room to coalesce. prefill_parallelism up reduces head-of-line stalls on large prompts.

maria: also check KV cache eviction metrics — if their 24k prompts are evicting many entries, prefill cost increases and effective throughput drops. add tag filter for tenant id on kv_cache_hits.

oliver: customer asked for quick mitigation — can we temporarily scale rp-west2-ded-17 up by +2 nodes to relieve pressure while we tune? ops?

deploy-bot: scale request queued: rp-west2-ded-17 +2 nodes (manual approval required).

raj: action items: 
1) run loadgen repro for 30m against a staging copy of their workload (raj)
2) canary batching config change on one scheduler ring (maria/infra) increasing max_batch_tokens & window
3) monitor prefills/sec, batch_size distribution, kv_cache_hit ratio; rollback if tail latency worsens (raj/maria)
4) temporary +2 nodes scale (ops)

sara: I've opened the customer escalation ticket and scheduled a 1h troubleshooting call at 20:00 UTC. I'll update them we're testing config canary + scaling. :thumbsup:

oliver: thanks team. if the canary improves batch_size median -> 8-10k tokens and raises token/s back towards baseline, we can roll to rest of pool. otherwise we'll investigate tenant isolation knobs.

maria: I'll provision the canary and run the first loadgen by 19:10 UTC. posting results in this thread.

raj: one more note — if continuous-batcher is in 'latency-sensitive' mode for that pool, it may aggressively close batches; check pool config `latency_target_ms`. bumping target slightly helps coalesce.

sara: copy. thanks all, I'll coordinate with customer and keep this thread updated.
